_meta.description: Seed events for synthetic fine-tuning generation. REBALANCED for partisan symmetry: every archetype appears for BOTH parties with the party-mirrored expected_effect, so expected_effect is symmetric under party swap. Good-news archetypes (endorsement, rally, convention, popular tax cut, jobs boom, foreign win) help THAT party for both. Bad-news archetypes (scandal, misconduct, impeachment, gaffe, debate loss, pardon) hurt THAT party for both. Ideological-overreach archetypes (far-left AND far-right) are tagged 'splits' symmetrically (valence != electoral effect). In-power exogenous shocks (recession, inflation, terror, casualties, disaster, domestic crisis) help the out-party, mirrored by which party holds power. The generator expands each seed ~20x and the DeepSeek->Gemini->Opus chain validates labels. expected_effect is a generation hint and a reviewer check, not a hard label.
_meta.rebalance_note: Replaces the prior asymmetric set where Republican-framed seeds were tagged helps_dem 11x but helps_rep only 1x. New set: helps_dem == helps_rep, and each party's events split helps/hurts/splits/neutral/realigns in identical proportions. Symmetry, not outcome-tuning.
_meta.magnitude_grounding: Phase 5, Step 5.1 (see DECISIONS.md). Bin midpoints rescaled to strong=0.0300, moderate=0.0175, mild=0.00875, slight=0.00300, neutral=0 -- matching electoral.core.types.BIN_MIDPOINTS. Grounded in VOTER panel ground truth (n=234 non-suppressed bloc/cycle cells): median per-bloc shift 0.0029, mean 0.0046, p90 0.0112, largest single-bloc shift ever measured 0.0286. Target bin distribution across a record's 15 bloc-level bins: 34% neutral, 31% slight, 28% mild, 6% moderate, 1% strong -- MEASURED from the panel's own empirical bin-magnitude distribution (data/ground_truth/panel_deltas.json, unweighted per-shock measured_delta, suppressed_flag==False, n=234; see scripts/synthetic/check_panel_target_calibration.py for the exact derivation and a rerunnable reproduction), not chosen by intuition. Corrected from an earlier intuition-derived 30/45/18/5/2 split that overstated 'slight' and understated 'mild' by ~10-14pp relative to what the panel actually shows; neutral/moderate/strong were already close in that version. 'strong' is still rare by construction, not a common label -- that part didn't change. These numbers are not read by the generator/reviewer scripts directly; they are duplicated into the DeepSeek and Gemini prompt text in scripts/synthetic/generate_deepseek.py and scripts/synthetic/gemini_review.py and must be kept in sync with this note by hand.

bin_distribution_target._note: Phase 5, Step 5.4 (added), corrected to panel-measured values in a later pass (see magnitude_grounding above for the before/after and scripts/synthetic/check_panel_target_calibration.py for the derivation -- rerun that script to reproduce these exact numbers from data/ground_truth/panel_deltas.json). Machine-readable copy of magnitude_grounding's target distribution above, added so electoral/metrics/synthetic_distribution.py has something to read instead of regex-parsing prose (that field's own text already admits this is a hand-synced duplication risk -- adding a second unstructured copy would make it worse, not better). Keys are the 5 sign-collapsed magnitude categories from electoral.core.types.MAGNITUDE_CATEGORIES. Values must sum to 1.0. If magnitude_grounding's prose numbers and this object ever disagree, this object is what code actually uses -- treat the prose as out of date, not this. ROUNDING: raw panel percentages (80/234, 72/234, 65/234, 14/234, 3/234 = 34.188%, 30.769%, 27.778%, 5.983%, 1.282%) rounded to the nearest whole percent (standard round-half-up; no category landed on a .5 tie) -- this happens to sum to exactly 100 with no remainder adjustment needed.

_meta.mobilization_field: Added 2026-08-03 (Phase 5, Step 5.1 follow-up -- flagged as a gap in the original Step 5.1 pass, not built there). Every seed now carries an explicit 'mobilization' property: 'mobilizing' (the event's negative/polarizing nature drives increased turnout/enthusiasm for one side -- court rulings on contested issues, impeachment, the ideological 'splits' archetypes, culture-war framing), 'depressing' (the event erodes confidence/enthusiasm for the affected party through persuasion/demoralization, no strong opposing-mobilization narrative -- scandals, gaffes, macro bad news, extremism-alienates-moderates), 'consolidating' (positive event reinforces existing support -- endorsements, rallies, good economic/foreign-policy news), or 'neutral' (genuinely bipartisan/low-salience, no partisan turnout dynamic -- matches expected_effect=='neutral' exactly, 4 seeds). This exists so the teacher model is TOLD the mobilization dynamic rather than inferring it from event tone -- inferring it from tone is exactly the confound that broke both prior SRP grounding attempts (see DECISIONS.md). Distribution: mobilizing=24, depressing=24, consolidating=12, neutral=4 (sums to 64); symmetric within party (helps_dem and helps_rep each split 12 mobilizing / 12 depressing / 6 consolidating / 2 neutral). Referenced explicitly in generate_deepseek.py's and gemini_review.py's prompts.
